title: Classic DLL injection
defender_note: Correlate a cross-process allocation + write + remote thread from one source process. Resolve the thread start address against loaded modules: an address outside any module is the strongest sign.

title: APC / early-bird injection
defender_note: A queued APC into another process followed by thread resumption is the core pattern. Watch for APCs queued right after CreateProcess with a suspended thread (early bird).

title: Process hollowing
defender_note: Look for a created-then-suspended child whose image is unmapped and rewritten, then resumed with a redirected entry point. Sysmon 25 (ProcessTampering) is the cheapest catch-all.

title: Thread execution hijacking
defender_note: Remote thread context reads and writes are rare outside debuggers. Compare the new instruction pointer with the module map of the target.

title: Section mapping / image reload
defender_note: Executable views of file mappings, especially when the backing file is in a temp directory or has no on-disk PE header, indicate reflective or manual mapping.

title: Keystroke capture
defender_note: Global keyboard hooks installed by unsigned binaries, plus high-frequency polling of GetAsyncKeyState, are the classic pair. Watch for hook installation outside interactive accessibility software.

title: Clipboard banking trojan
defender_note: A process that polls the clipboard and rewrites it with attacker-controlled wallet addresses or IBANs. Sequence-number polling loops are the tell.

title: Desktop screenshot capture
defender_note: GDI captures of the whole desktop from a non-interactive process, often followed by file writes or network uploads.

title: Ransomware encryption flow
defender_note: High-rate file rewrites with renamed extensions, entropy jumps and shadow-copy deletion. Alert on encryption APIs combined with recursive enumeration in user data paths.

title: LSASS credential dumping
defender_note: Granted access to lsass.exe with read rights (0x1010 / 0x1410) is the highest-fidelity signal. Alert on any non-security process opening LSASS and on minidump writes to temp paths.

title: Token theft and impersonation
defender_note: Token duplication from a SYSTEM process followed by process creation is privilege escalation. Correlate with 4672/4688 and unusual parent-child relationships.

title: Service-based persistence

mitre.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

defender_note: Event 7045 service installs with binaries outside trusted paths, or a service name that mimics a driver. Check the creating process and service account.

title: Run key / startup persistence

mitre.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

defender_note: Writes to Run/RunOnce or the Startup folder by non-installer processes. Compare the value path with the writing binary's directory and signature.

title: Reverse shell over Winsock
defender_note: Outbound socket from a non-browser process immediately followed by child-process creation with redirected std handles. Destination reputation and volume matter more than the API list.

title: HTTP downloader / dropper
defender_note: A user-mode download of an executable into temp/appdata followed by execution. Proxy logs, URL reputation and file-write-then-execute sequences all detect this.

title: DNS tunnelling / TXT exfiltration
defender_note: High-volume, high-entropy DNS queries with long labels from a single host. DNS server logs and passive DNS give better fidelity than endpoint API telemetry.

title: AMSI tampering
defender_note: Any non-security process resolving amsi.dll and changing the protection of AmsiScanBuffer is almost always malicious. Enable AMSI provider ETW and script-block logging.

title: ETW patching
defender_note: Writes into ntdll!EtwEventWrite or calls to NtTraceControl that disable providers. Monitor image protection changes on ntdll and early process writes into its code section.

title: EDR userland unhooking
defender_note: Mapping a fresh copy of ntdll from disk and copying its .text over the loaded module restores clean syscall stubs. Typical of malware that expects inline hooks.

title: UAC bypass via token / COM

mitre.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control

defender_note: Elevated process creation without a consent prompt, especially via auto-elevating COM objects or token duplication into a medium-integrity parent.

title: Driver loading for kernel execution
defender_note: Service creation pointing at a .sys file followed by NtLoadDriver. Driver signature enforcement and vulnerable-driver blocklists are the primary controls.

title: SMB / admin share lateral movement
defender_note: SMB connections to ADMIN$/C$ followed by service creation or file copies. 4624 type 3 logons, 5140 share access and service installs on the target host tell the story.

title: HTTPS exfiltration
defender_note: Large outbound POST bodies from a host that normally only browses. Look at bytes-out per destination and TLS SNI/JA3 consistency.
